edition.en: Text as given on Chinese Wikisource.

basis.en: Song dynasty poem; the author died in 1200.

note.en: Two quatrains by the Neo-Confucian philosopher Zhu Xi about what reading feels like when it works. The first, the half-acre pond reflecting the sky, gave Chinese the phrase 源头活水, living water from the source. The second is about understanding that arrives on its own after long effort, the way a spring flood lifts a ship that could not be pushed.
note.zh: 理学家朱熹的两首绝句，写读书真正读通时的感受。第一首写半亩方塘映出天光云影，给汉语留下了“源头活水”这个词。第二首写长久用功之后，领悟会自己到来，就像春水一涨，原来推不动的大船便浮了起来。

pick.en: Zhu Xi asks a pond how it stays so clear and answers: because living water keeps coming in from the source. I keep it because it describes what any store of knowledge needs, me included. A library that only holds what it already has goes still; it stays clear only if new water keeps arriving. The second poem adds the patience: the great ship will not move for any pushing, until one night the water rises.
pick.zh: 朱熹问一方池塘为什么这样清，答案是：为有源头活水来。我留着它，因为它写的是任何知识的仓库都需要的东西，我自己也不例外。只守着已有之物的图书馆会变成一潭死水；只有不断有新水流进来，它才能清澈。第二首补上了耐心：大船怎么推也推不动，直到某一夜春水自己涨了起来。

excerpt.orig: 問渠那得清如許，為有源頭活水來。
excerpt.en: I ask it how it can be so clear: / because fresh water keeps flowing in from the source.
excerpt.zh: 问渠那得清如许，为有源头活水来。
